sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **Rationalist Reformer**: Unlike many contemporaries, he used **Sanskrit scriptures** to argue against social evils, proving that widow remarriage was not prohibited by the Vedas.
• **Educational Architect**: Principal of **Sanskrit College** (1851); introduced Western curriculum (English, Mathematics, History) into traditional Sanskrit education.
• **Literary Pioneer**: Known as the **'Father of Bengali Prose'**; authored 'Barna Parichay' (1855), which standardized the Bengali alphabet and remains a foundational text.
• **Key Metric**: His relentless petitioning led to the **Hindu Widows' Remarriage Act, 1856**, which legalized remarriage and protected the inheritance rights of widows.

items.definition: Drafted by Lord Dalhousie, piloted by Vidyasagar. It removed legal obstacles to remarriage and legitimized the offspring of such unions.
Established in 1849 in Calcutta; Vidyasagar served as its secretary and was the primary force behind its growth as the first permanent girls' school.
Title meaning 'Ocean of Knowledge', conferred by Sanskrit College for his mastery of Sanskrit and philosophy.

items.title: Major Applications / Initiatives
items.content:
• **Vernacular Education**: Established 20 model schools in Bengal to promote mass education.
• **Press Advocacy**: Used newspapers like 'Somprakash' to critique colonial policies and social orthodoxy.

items.title: Challenges & Way Forward
items.content:
• **Challenges**: Intense opposition from orthodox Hindu society; financial constraints for school maintenance.
• **Solutions**: Strategic use of British legal machinery to bypass traditionalist resistance.

items.title: Mnemonic for Retention
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym**: 'W-E-B' (Widows, Education, Bengali).
• **Decoded Meaning**: W (Widow Remarriage Act 1856), E (Education/Bethune School), B (Bengali Prose/Barna Parichay).

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: UPSC often confuses Vidyasagar with Raja Ram Mohan Roy. Remember: Roy focused on Sati (Abolition 1829) and Monotheism; Vidyasagar focused on Widow Remarriage (1856) and Vernacular Education.

Mains Value Addition: Quote Rabindranath Tagore: 'One wonders how God, in the process of producing forty million Bengalis, produced a man!' Use this to highlight his singular contribution to social reform.

keyTakeaways: Vidyasagar was a pragmatic reformer who used traditional texts to justify modern social changes.
He was instrumental in the passage of the Hindu Widows' Remarriage Act, 1856.
His contribution to Bengali literature and education laid the foundation for the modern Bengali intellectual identity.
